changes.before: Update editable profile fields without changing the ID or mutating the original object.
changes.after: Allow small text updates while keeping the profile's ID unchanged.

before: Pick creates a type containing only chosen properties from another type.
Partial makes every property of a type optional. A patch can then describe only the fields being changed.
Readonly prevents assignment through a typed reference. It is a shallow compiler restriction, not Object.freeze.

For the exercise, ProfilePatch permits name and bio. Return a new profile with supplied text fields applied, keep omitted fields, and preserve id. Treat an explicit undefined field like an omitted field; an empty string is a deliberate update.
Use the allowed fields explicitly rather than assuming a type annotation removes unexpected runtime fields.
after: Pick makes a type from selected properties of another type. It describes which properties are allowed; it does not remove fields from an existing object.
Partial makes each property optional. A patch is a small set of changes, so it can contain only the fields you want to update.
The example supplies a new note but no title. Applying that update should keep the old title. A missing property does not mean delete the old value.
Readonly prevents assigning to a property through that type. It is a shallow checking rule, so it does not freeze nested objects while the program runs.

ProfilePatch allows name and bio. Return a new profile with those supplied text updates, keep the ID, and keep omitted values. In this exercise, undefined also means keep the old value. Empty text is a real update.
Read and copy only the allowed fields. A type description does not strip unexpected fields from data while JavaScript runs.

before.question: Pick<Profile, "name" | "bio"> is a type. Does it remove id from an existing object at runtime?
choices: No; runtime code must choose which fields to copy
Yes; it deletes id as soon as the file runs
Yes; Partial then deletes every omitted field
before.explanation: Utility types describe allowed shapes during typechecking. They do not execute data transformations or sanitize external objects.

after.question: Does Pick<Profile, "name" | "bio"> remove id from an actual object?
choices: No, running code must choose what to copy
Yes, it deletes id when the file runs
Yes, Partial deletes every omitted field
after.explanation: These tools describe types. They do not change actual objects.

changes.before: Strict compiler tests required for forbidden patch ID and readonly writes. Runtime unexpected-ID test intentionally supplies a value JavaScript may receive despite compile-time types. Partial permits undefined under this runner configuration; behavior explicitly preserves old text for undefined.
changes.after: This lesson's settings permit explicit undefined in the patch. The requested behavior keeps the old text for that value and rejects ID updates.
